Keep useful starting units. An unavailable Noble, Mage or artillery slot can temporarily be another spear or archer; do not wait for a perfect army to fight a necessary early war.
Shadow-walkers are not Sisters of Avelorn
The army keeps a conventional screen and armour-piercing support. Do not assume the expensive bow unit replaces every tactical role.
Generic company
The supporting version uses a recruitable Princess, not another copy of Alith. The walkers are faction recruits, but Alith’s personal speed, ammo and unique skill effects do not follow them.
Under Smart Autoresolve
Accept a result based on actual losses and the next enemy turn. Stalk, poison, healing and decoys are not assigned a guessed numerical multiplier in this guide.
Affordable opening
Three walkers are a staged first investment, not a requirement to disband a starting specialist. A bolt slot can stay an archer until the Workshop is affordable.
Alternatives, not simultaneous armies

Early, mid and late are progression stages of the same evolving company; the specialist template is an optional variant for a chosen second force, and the home template is emergency local relief. Do not treat all five templates as separate permanent armies or clone Alith and his embedded Noble into more than one.
plan: Deploy an anchor
Keep the shielded escort together. Place bolt throwers where they can shoot without putting the entire army in one narrow corridor. Give walkers a nearby fallback position.
Use two hunter sections
Divide walkers into two manageable groups on or beside the flanks. Start within support distance; do not deploy every unit in isolation merely because it can hide.
Break one threat first
Use Alith and concentrated missiles on the enemy unit that would disrupt your plan. Slow or pin it with the caster, then switch targets after it is neutralised.
After contact
Keep reserves off the initial line. Commit White Lions, Swordmasters or the flying support to a specific problem; restore the formation with pause/slow speed when necessary.
